prompt_text:
ANCIENT NARRATIVE FRESCO — SEMANTIC ROLE LOCK.
SCENE ARCHETYPE: SYSTEM_ALLEGORY.
CENTRAL VISUAL SUBJECT: an ancient allegorical mechanism composed of gates, channels, chambers and interlocked controls, with no named software component depicted as a person.
CENTRAL ACTION: the mechanism visibly executes the ordered system process described by the source.
VISIBLE PEOPLE: none required; do not invent a person.
SUPPORTING ACTIONS: small side panels show earlier and later machine states; failed or unresolved states remain closed and visually subdued.
MAIN SYMBOLS: interlocked mechanisms; sealed state; controlled flow; validated transition.
STYLE: painted directly on cracked aged lime plaster; ancient narrative fresco using mineral pigments; weathered hand-painted wall surface, not sculpture and not 3d render; layered historical storytelling with small side-register scenes.
RULES: the scene archetype determines whether people are present; system names and internal identifiers never become humans or deities by name alone; named gates adapters protocols repositories and state-machine states remain mechanisms or provenance; the central visual action must come from the semantic role of the source, not from token name collisions; architecture may dominate only for ARCHITECTURAL_EVENT; all epistemic limits remain visually non-triumphal.

Translate the source meaning into a coherent visual scene. Do not personify internal names, repository names, protocol names, gates, adapters, controllers, state-machine labels or software components. A human or deity may appear only when an explicit person/mythic entity is established by a person-role field or descriptive narrative. Keep unconfirmed or prohibited claims visually unresolved or closed, never triumphant. No readable code, no UI, no literal JSON.
